slides.heading: Choosing for vs while
slides.body: Choosing for vs while is part of Definite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Choosing for vs while
slides.body: Use a for loop when the number of repetitions is known or when processing a sequence. Use a while loop when repetition depends on a changing condition.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Choosing between for and while is like choosing a route: use for when the path is listed, and while when you continue until a condition changes.

annotations.note: This line starts a loop that processes each value in a sequence.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use for loops when you want to repeat through a known range or sequence.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use a for loop to print each item in a short list.
slides.hint: Write for item in items: then print(item).
